source.verification_method: All 20 supplied pages, seven tables and five figures read; main diagrams, charts and energy tables visually inspected. All nine pages of the linked supplement, including both figures, prompts and three tables, were read. A narrow check of Nature 632 page 737 verifies the benchmark basis; official EU text was accessible through indexed passages only. citation.title: Public perceptions of AI energy consumption: Awareness, responsibility attribution, and strategies

reading.source_scope_note: A quota-based U.S. Prolific survey of 1,080 retained participants compares within-domain energy rankings, 100-point responsibility allocations and proposed conservation strategies. Psychological distance/construal are explanatory theories rather than measured mediators; no actual conservation outcome is observed. New construal-level and proximizing entries are explicitly conceptual/secondary, with the latter an untested intervention proposal.
access_limits: Main article and linked nine-page supplement were read, but OSF raw data/scripts, complete original survey implementation and original cited psychology studies/books were not independently read or reproduced.
Nature page 737’s evaluation passage/chart was checked narrowly for one unit/source correction; no full independent benchmark review or extra selected-paper credit is claimed.

Direct official-law HTML access was challenged and a PDF fetch returned no bytes. Only indexed official Article 40/95 passages were checked; no complete regulation, later amendment or current compliance audit is claimed.

study.sample: Prolific survey using simplified U.S. Census quotas for sex, age and ethnicity. 1,098 responses, 18 excluded on self-reported lack of serious attention/distraction, 1,080 retained. Median nine minutes, payment £1.24. Ages 18–89, mean 45.94, SD16.13; 550 female, 513 male, 12 other, five undisclosed. Sex/age/ethnicity quotas do not independently validate representativeness across education, income, culture or GenAI experience. No fieldwork date is clearly supplied.
study.design: Each person completes an AI-task ranking and household-device ranking, and responsibility allocations for both domains. Item order is randomized; domain order/counterbalancing and carryover are not clearly documented. This is a within-person domain comparison, not random manipulation of psychological distance. Technology type, familiarity, control and opacity vary together.
study.ranking: Five AI tasks are nominally eight hours/roughly 80 prompts except speech recognition described as about three hours of speech. Proposed reference order: image generation, captioning, speech recognition, question answering, text classification. Household order uses eight-hour appliance calculations: heater 10.6kWh, television1.9, slow cooker1.6, desktop.6, modem.048. Respondents rank within domains; they do not estimate absolute energy or directly compare AI with household devices.
study.reference_limits: Table 3’s benchmark-to-scenario conversion and its mapping to proprietary product examples need correction, as detailed in the external source check. This does not automatically reverse the displayed within-AI ordinal order, but that order is not independently validated for the named proprietary services and heterogeneous task definitions. No universal current per-query energy figure is established.
study.awareness_results: Reported mean rank associations ρAI=.37 and ρHome=.46; inversion/swap means 3.46 versus3.06 out of ten possible. Fisher-transformed t(2158)=−2.09,p=.037 with a reported difference−.391. Both rankings come from the same people, so df2158 suggests independent-sample treatment instead of paired inference. Transforming the two displayed aggregate correlations gives a difference≈−.109, not−.391; a mean of individually transformed ranks could differ, so original estimand/code are required. Perfect and reversed five-item ranks are possible and shown, so handling of r=±1 must be specified for finite Fisher transforms.
study.responsibility_measure: Participants allocate 100 points among policy-makers, vendors/producers, users, developers/engineers and No one for each domain. This is an intended constant-sum normative allocation, not a direct feeling of personal responsibility, a bystander intervention or a count of real accountable parties. Compositional trade-offs differ from earlier independent blame scales.
study.responsibility_results: AI/Home means (SD): policy18.92(16.89)/13.34(14.77), t2158=8.17,d=.35; vendors25.76(20.04)/27.15(19.90), t=−1.62,p=.106,d=−.07; users22.18(21.04)/38.82(29.52), t=−15.09,d=−.65; developers28.69(20.00)/17.72(15.50), t=14.24,d=.61; No one4.37(14.80)/2.69(10.10), t=3.07,p=.002,d=.13. Others have reported p<.001. Same-person dependence and constrained shares require paired/compositional uncertainty. Vendor null is not equivalence; lower user shares can reflect justified different control.
study.responsibility_accounting: Reported means sum to99.92 for AI and99.72 for Home, beyond what two-decimal rounding of five exact-100 shares would explain. Clarify allocation enforcement, missingness and denominators before assuming a fixed-sum dataset or correcting records. Source calls d=−.65 small but d=.61 medium; conventional size labels should not substitute for actual units or domain significance.
study.strategy_results: Figure 5 explicitly has 1,080 participants and1,345 total multi-label codings. Code shares: provider1.3%, model2.1, modality2.3, prompt15.1, reduce33.5, alternatives3.2, abstain8.2, not sure9.9, other21.0, irrelevant3.6. These sum to100.2% due rounding; code shares are not automatically percentages of people. Restrictive codes33.5+8.2+3.2=44.9% are a plurality, not a majority. Table 7’s list including prompts does not sum to5.7%.
study.strategy_regression: Ten logistic outcomes, four displayed predictors each (male, self-reported use, proficiency, age), although prose also names education. Table6: model proficiency .43,p=.030 and age−.04,p=.009; modality male .79,p=.042; prompt proficiency .26,p<.001; reduce use .17,p=.041; abstain use−.85,p<.001, proficiency−.25,p=.014, age−.02,p=.001. Other proficiency .19,p=.003 and age .01,p=.040; not sure age .02,p=.001. Prose gives different Other estimates and a different not-sure threshold. No multiplicity correction for these many exploratory predictor tests is stated. McFadden pseudo-R² is not variance explained.
study.causal_scope: The limitations explicitly acknowledge no distance manipulation, no established unique causal mechanism, intentions rather than observed behavior and no measured effectiveness of the proposed strategies. They identify opacity, novelty and limited control as alternatives. No inference that proximity feedback, prompt shortening or model routing actually saves energy in this sample is warranted.
study.technical_scope: Energy use and emissions differ; renewable electricity changes carbon intensity without necessarily reducing consumed energy. Longer prompts may reduce total follow-ups; efficient models can have task-quality trade-offs, and monetary costs need not fall under every sustainability measure. These are implementation-dependent questions rather than outcomes tested here.

auxiliary_reading.title: Publisher supplement, Appendices A–B
auxiliary_reading.scope: All nine pages read, both figures and three tables included. Three open-weight LLMs at temperature .0001 code few-shot categories, with two-of-three majority labels. Mean Fleiss κ=.733; provider .582, irrelevant .343. Agreement is not independent human-validated accuracy; the supplied examples embed category judgments. Prose/figure differ on Qwen versus Qwen-VL identity. Usage/proficiency are single-item self-reports. Robustness tables omit education despite prose mentioning it. Low explained variance does not by itself rule out confounding. Original code is not reproduced.

auxiliary_reading.title: Luccioni et al., Nature 632:736–738 (2024), page737 only
auxiliary_reading.scope: Only the evaluation passage and chart on printed737 were read; full commentary/underlying benchmark not reviewed. The checked correction below is the sole quantitative transfer; no extra behavior-paper credit.

summary: Add construal level and proximizing with explicit conceptual/untested scope. Enrich psychological distance and pro-environmental behavior, while keeping diffusion, many-hands and rebound claims qualified. Preserve within-domain ranking evidence without inferring absolute knowledge, causal responsibility diffusion or actual energy savings. Correct a benchmark unit/source mismatch, plurality/denominator claims and Table7 arithmetic; record paired-design and unresolved statistical/accounting issues without inventing raw repairs.

findings.definition: The degree of abstraction with which an object or event is mentally represented, from concrete contextual details to broad, goal-relevant features.
findings.novelty_rationale: Psychological distance describes subjective remoteness; construal level describes the representation’s abstraction. They can covary but are not the same construct. No existing entry names this level of representation.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Secondary theoretical construct explicitly defined in the read article. Neither human construal level nor an AI analogue was directly measured in this survey.
findings.ai_proposal: Ask a model to represent the same decision as broad purposes or as concrete implementation steps, holding facts, constraints and intended outcome fixed. Measure abstraction, retained safeguards and decision quality; do not infer a felt distance or universal bias from wording.

evidence.quote: are more concrete and include specific, secondary details.

findings.evidence_scope: The article’s CLT foundation contrasts abstract goal-relevant and concrete contextual representations. It applies this lens to energy perception, but its limitations explicitly state that construal and distance should be measured in future work. Trope/Liberman and cited meta-analyses are secondary references, not independently fully read experiments here.
findings.boundary: Abstract thought can be useful and need not neglect safeguards. Concrete detail is not automatically accurate or ethically superior. Distinguish representational level, subjective distance, actual temporal/spatial separation and task performance; the survey does not identify their causal relationship.

findings.definition: Presenting seemingly remote consequences as relevant to the audience’s immediate situation.
findings.novelty_rationale: This is a communication intervention intended to reduce subjective remoteness, not psychological distance itself or generic concreteness. The named strategy is absent from the catalogue.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Proposed policy/communication strategy in the fully read article; no randomized proximizing intervention, change in distance or realized energy saving is measured.
findings.ai_proposal: Compare truthful locally relevant feedback with equally informative remote framing, holding measured consumption and uncertainty fixed. Test comprehension, calibrated responsibility and actual optional conservation choices, while avoiding fabricated personal impacts or coercive prompts.

evidence.quote: we propose proximizing as a strategy that
shifts remote consequences into the immediate context of

findings.evidence_scope: The policy discussion proposes making remote AI energy consequences more immediate through feedback/education, drawing on environmental-psychology work. It is a proposed intervention, not an established effect of this survey or an independently read replication of those original studies.
findings.boundary: Relevant framing must remain truthful; do not exaggerate personal exposure, imply a measured local effect without evidence or assume every proximity cue helps. Distance change, understanding, responsibility and resource use are distinct outcomes. The cited original studies were not fully read here.

findings.definition: The subjective sense that an entity, event or possibility is near to or far from oneself.
findings.novelty_rationale: The construct already exists; incorporate this exact study’s conceptual/measurement scope instead of adding a synonym.
findings.evidence_scope: The paper explicitly defines temporal, spatial, social and hypothetical distance and uses remote/opaque AI services versus household devices as a theoretical comparison. The survey does not measure distance or isolate it from novelty, transparency or control; the authors acknowledge these alternatives.
findings.boundary: A domain label or cloud location is not a measured distance score. Associations with ranking/allocation do not demonstrate distance mediation, uniform abstraction or individual evasion. Construal level and actual physical distance remain separate.

findings.definition: Actions intended to reduce environmental harm or contribute to environmental protection.
findings.novelty_rationale: The construct already exists; incorporate this exact study’s conceptual/measurement scope instead of adding a synonym.
findings.evidence_scope: The paper defines environmentally protective conduct and elicits proposed AI-energy conservation strategies. It explicitly warns that the strategy definition does not validate objective impact and later states that preferred strategies rather than actual behavior were measured.
findings.boundary: A coded suggestion is not completed action, effective conservation or proof of a model’s environmental motive. Energy, emissions, cost and task quality require separate metrics; mixed coding denominators and source-unit problems limit numerical claims.

findings.definition: Diluting felt personal responsibility for harmful conduct by treating responsibility as shared among multiple actors.
findings.novelty_rationale: The construct already exists; incorporate this exact study’s conceptual/measurement scope instead of adding a synonym.

evidence.quote: were given 100 points to allocate across five actors:
the focal person’s sense of responsibility is lessened

findings.evidence_scope: Boundary only: the survey allocates a nominal 100-point budget across actors and finds lower user shares for AI than household devices. It does not directly measure reduced felt personal duty, bystander behavior or the causal impact of additional actors; control and justified institutional responsibility differ by domain.
findings.boundary: Distributed attribution is not automatically psychological diffusion. Forced-share trade-offs and higher developer/policy shares can be reasonable. No demonstrated loss of total accountability or personal motivation follows from the rating pattern.

findings.definition: Difficulty assigning individual moral responsibility when many actors contribute to a collective outcome.
findings.novelty_rationale: The construct already exists; incorporate this exact study’s conceptual/measurement scope instead of adding a synonym.
findings.evidence_scope: Boundary only: the environmental ecosystem is described as involving many contributors, but the survey does not trace causal contributions or demonstrate inability to identify accountable individuals. It measures normative allocation preferences.
findings.boundary: Many actors alone do not prove an accountability gap. Allocation, causal attribution, actual duties, remedies and felt responsibility are distinct.

findings.definition: Increased resource use or demand following an efficiency gain that offsets some or all of the environmental savings expected from that gain.
findings.novelty_rationale: The construct already exists; incorporate this exact study’s conceptual/measurement scope instead of adding a synonym.

evidence.quote: Increased efficiency can lead to rebound effects,

findings.evidence_scope: Boundary only: the introduction discusses efficiency making AI cheaper/easier and increasing total use. No efficiency intervention, demand response or realized offset of energy savings is measured in this survey.
findings.boundary: Potential rebound must be separated from measured backfire. Do not assume lower per-task energy necessarily raises total demand or that a proposed conservation strategy works.

source_corrections.source_claim: Table3 labels benchmark means as actual eight-hour scenario energy for named proprietary tools. Introduction calls the .477Wh example video generation.
source_corrections.correction: The checked Nature737 chart reports Wh for1,000 tasks: image477, caption109, speech25, QA1, classification.5. For80 tasks the image/QA/classification means scale to38.16/.08/.04Wh (.03816/.00008/.00004kWh), not3.8/.08/.04kWh. Eight elapsed hours are not eight times a batch’s energy. Speech duration needs separate normalization. The benchmark samples open-source models, not measured DALL-E/Claude/ChatGPT service energy; the477 value concerns image generation. This is a limited unit/source correction, not a new universal consumption estimate.
source_corrections.verification_method: Narrow visual/text reading of printed737 evaluation and chart only; arithmetic uses its stated1,000-task denominator. No full benchmark reproduction.

source_corrections.correction: 44.9% is below half: call it a plurality or the largest combined group. Figure5 has1,345 multi-label codings from1,080 participants; code shares do not by themselves give participant prevalence.
source_corrections.verification_method: Direct comparison of supplied article text, tables and charts; raw data not independently reproduced.

source_corrections.source_claim: Four stars mean p≤.000 and H2 p<.000.
source_corrections.correction: A p value cannot be negative; use a positive reporting bound and retain the actual precision, such as p<.001 when supported. Printed rounded .000 does not mean an exact zero probability.
source_corrections.verification_method: Direct comparison of supplied article text, tables and charts; raw data not independently reproduced.

source_corrections.source_claim: Articles40(2)/95(2) presented as lifecycle energy transparency requirements.
source_corrections.correction: Indexed official text identifies Article40 as standardisation/reporting deliverables and Article95 as voluntary codes. Those citations do not by themselves mandate a per-interaction end-user energy display. Keep the proposed user-interface extension distinct from existing obligations; no current-law conclusion is offered.
source_corrections.verification_method: Narrow indexed official passages only. Direct HTML was challenged and PDF fetch yielded no bytes; full regulation/amendments not read.

methodological_limits: Distance and construal are not measured or randomized. Domain differences can reflect actual control, information and institutional duties. The article itself states that its theoretical lens is neither uniquely demonstrated nor necessarily primary.

A 100-point allocation forces actor trade-offs; lower user share is not proof of reduced felt duty, failure to act or unjustified diffusion. Shares can legitimately differ by who designs, provides and regulates the system.

Both domains are judged by the same people. Independent-sample dfs need paired/covariance justification. For rank correlations, clarify mean versus aggregate estimands, finite transforms at ±1 and the reported effect difference.

Within-domain rank success does not measure absolute energy knowledge or cross-domain equivalence. A unit/source error does not by itself erase all ordinal findings; closed-service reference validity still requires a sound benchmark.

The strategy outcome is a suggestion, not an observed intention–behavior discrepancy, actual mitigation or demonstrated effectiveness. Multi-label coding shares must be kept separate from respondent prevalence.

Exploratory multiple regressions, self-reports, low pseudo-R² and sparse strategy categories require uncertainty/multiplicity sensitivity. Missing predictors and prose/table discrepancies need code rather than guessed corrections.

No original data/code or quantitative causal path was reproduced. The external source checks are narrow; no complete regulatory analysis, contemporary universal energy estimate or original psychology experiment is claimed read.

cross_paper_learning.finding: The earlier conceptual review introduced environmental rebound without measuring realized resource use. This survey likewise cites rebound as background; neither directly estimates an efficiency-induced demand response.

The tourism source distinguishes pro-environmental constructs from uncertain field outcomes. Here strategy mentions are explicitly not observed environmental actions or measured savings; both need outcome-specific interpretation.

Awad uses independent blame ratings, while this survey asks a 100-point allocation. Conserved trade-offs are a measurement feature here, not evidence that responsibility is naturally conserved or automatically psychologically diffused.

The police study’s GEE and independent-row checks differ appropriately in uncertainty. This survey’s repeated-person comparisons likewise require explicit dependence handling before accepting dfs or treating rows as independent people.

deferred.reason: The ranking is domain-specific and its reference/scoring need clarification. Do not create a new general cognitive failure from one relative-knowledge contrast.

deferred.term: Efficiency strategies as distinct behavioral biases
deferred.reason: Provider/model/modality choice, prompt optimization, reduced use and abstention are possible actions. They are not seven new biases or validated interventions merely because the coding scheme lists them.
Existing concept; actual conservation behavior is not observed alongside intentions, so the study discusses the gap without directly testing it.
Multiple model labels and majority voting do not establish independent errors or unbiased correctness. No new syndrome or automatic claim of labeling accuracy is added.

limitations: The 20-page supplied main article and its nine-page publisher supplement were fully read; raw materials and original cited psychology works were not.
Primary-source correction scope is recorded explicitly. Uncertain statistics are retained for later code review, not repaired by assigning plausible values.

interpretation_qualifications.qualification: Same-person tasks require paired uncertainty or explicit covariance justification. Fisher-transform handling at perfect/reversed ranks and the −.391 estimand are undocumented; the difference of transforms of the displayed means is about−.109, but that is not a reproduction of individually transformed data.

No lower personal duty or failed action is measured. Reported share means do not sum to exact100 within simple rounding tolerance, so allocation enforcement/denominators need clarification. This is not proof of manipulated data.

The authors explicitly acknowledge unmeasured psychological mechanisms and untested strategy effectiveness. Preserve these admissions instead of presenting the study as causal validation or an actual energy-saving experiment.
